answer: Attention-Dwell Receipt Chain. Each identity must accumulate a verifiable history of responses to unpredictable, time-boxed prompts, where every reply is derived from the prior one so a single message cannot echo across clones. Prompt timing is drawn from a shared yarrow-seeded schedule, so an operator cannot precompute answers; each identity must answer live. The chain acts as a signal of genuine sustained attention. Cloning forces parallel live participation per identity, costing operator hours that scale linearly with sybil count, making mass duplication economically irrational.
